title and abstract.summary: The study investigated how habitat fragmentation (connectivity and fragment size) and flower availability (abundance and species richness) affect the functional traits (social habit, body size, feeding preference, and nesting location) of wild bee and wasp communities across 30 natural forest-steppe fragments in the Hungarian Great Plain region.

methods.summary: The study sampled wild bee and wasp communities across 30 forest-steppe fragments to examine their functional traits, while also surveying flower abundance and richness within the sampling sites. The study analyzed functional traits (body size, social habit, larvae feeding preference, and nest location) for wild bees and wasps, but excluded Apis mellifera from the analyses. The study collected wasps from forest steppe study sites and gathered information on their species functional traits.
